semantics.note: 'More confident than ever' plus 'won't' is a firm, high-confidence forecast, so it is scored. 'This year' means calendar 2024.

contract.note: Reading 'land' as a public release of a model named GPT-5 is the ordinary reading. The result does not depend on any contested interpretation.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (Dec 31, 2024) has passed. OpenAI's dated announcement puts GPT-5's first public release on Aug 7, 2025, and the packet shows no release of a model named GPT-5 in 2024. The forecast held.

attribution.note: This is Marcus's own sign-off line, written in the third person in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Betting' is firm language and is scored. The claim depends on GPT-5's release ('whenever it finally drops'), so it is a conditional forecast, which the drafter's condition already preserves.

contract.note: 'A bunch' and 'wacky' are vague. Reading them as recurring, conspicuous launch-era errors is a fair, ordinary reading. Excluding errors caused by the image model is fair.

evidence.note: Dated rollout post (Aug 7, 2025) shows the release condition was met. It is evidence of the condition, not of the outcome.
OpenAI said in Sep 2025 that GPT-5 hallucinations still occur, though less often. This is a company admission against its own interest.
The launch system card reports nonzero hallucination rates for GPT-5 across benchmarks, alongside large reductions from earlier models.
Guardian's own test of GPT-5 produced a basic letter-counting error, and the article reports other text errors such as the 'blueberry' count. The map misspellings may come from the image model.

reviews.rationale: GPT-5 was released on Aug 7, 2025. Launch-era evidence (OpenAI's system card, OpenAI's own admission, and a Guardian test) shows continuing hallucinations and conspicuous basic errors. Fewer hallucinations is consistent with 'continue to hallucinate.'
